page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A1.160 is a bare-metal server configuration based on the Arm64 processor architecture. It is equipped with Ampere Altra processors providing 160 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed 3.0 GHz clock frequency. The architecture allocates a single hardware thread per core, eliminating core-sharing overhead and resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading environments. System memory totals 1024 GB, establishing an allocation of 6.4 GB of RAM per physical core.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. All persistent data workflows require network-attached storage architectures. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The absence of a hypervisor layer provides direct bare-metal access to CPU and memory subsystems, ensuring deterministic execution latency across all 160 cores.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high physical core count paired with 1024 GB of memory yields qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads. The platform is engineered to support container orchestration clusters, distributed web serving systems, large-scale CI/CD build environments, video transcoding pipelines, and native Arm software development.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.A1.160 is a dedicated bare-metal server powered by the Arm64 architecture. It features 160 physical cores using Ampere Altra processors operating at a sustained 3.0 GHz clock speed, configured with one thread per core for deterministic multi-core performance without virtualization overhead. The server provides 1024 GB of memory, equating to 6.4 GB of RAM per dedicated core. There are no discrete GPUs or onboard local storage devices bundled with the configuration, directing persistent I/O workloads to external block or network storage solutions. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With high core count density and consistent per-core execution, BM.Standard.A1.160 offers strong resource efficiency for compute-heavy parallel tasks, container orchestration, microservices architectures, continuous integration build clusters, and native Arm development environments.
